Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=4 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) & ⇒ & v=-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 4x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =4x\cdot (-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))-\int (-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))\cdot 4\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }4x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{4}{3}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi }+\frac{4}{3}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi }+\frac{4}{9}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}(2\pi \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(6\pi )-0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0))+\frac{4}{9}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(6\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}(2\pi \cdot 1-0\cdot 1)+\frac{4}{9}(0-0) \\  & =-\frac{8\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
